# Bogie

> A Go API service, from zero to production. Bogie is a command-line tool that scaffolds an API-only, Postgres-only Go service with generators (new, g scaffold, g model, g controller, g job, g seed, g authentication, g policy, g config) that also wire the code in, and model:sync to carry a hand-written migration into the model, queries, store and factory. It builds on Gin, sqlc with pgx, goose, River (opt-in) and Kamal, and generated apps test with Ginkgo and Gomega. Generated apps never import Bogie itself; the only bogie-go library they use is credentials. MIT licensed, v0.7.0. Generated apps need Go 1.26 or newer (the CLI itself builds with 1.25) and Docker with Compose v2 for the local Postgres.

Install: `go install github.com/bogie-go/bogie@latest`. Then `bogie new blog && cd blog && make up && bogie db:prepare && bogie server`.

Every generated app follows six rules: ctx first on anything doing I/O; interfaces declared where they are consumed; the models package imports nothing third-party; constructors return (T, error); *gin.Context never travels below the controllers; no util, helpers or common packages. Each app ships an AGENTS.md with the rules, the commands and a recipe per task.

## Guides

- [Getting started](https://bogie-go.com/docs/getting-started.html): Install Bogie, generate a new service, and get it migrating, seeded and serving.
- [Models and migrations](https://bogie-go.com/docs/models.html): Add a table with g model, change one with g migration, and run it through db:*.
- [Seeds](https://bogie-go.com/docs/seeds.html): Plain Go seeds with g seed; db:seed runs every one, every time, so each is safe to run twice.
- [Resources, controllers and routing](https://bogie-go.com/docs/controllers.html): Scaffold a whole resource or write a controller by hand, and see how either gets registered.
- [Static files and error pages](https://bogie-go.com/docs/static-files.html): Files in public/, embedded in the binary and served below the router; the 404 and 500 pages.
- [Authentication](https://bogie-go.com/docs/authentication.html): Guard a route group with a middleware: a shared secret, a bearer token, or a machine client's key.
- [Authorization](https://bogie-go.com/docs/authorization.html): Since v0.7.0, bogie g policy writes plain-Go authorization: a denial is 403, and a token may carry a role claim.
- [Services](https://bogie-go.com/docs/services.html): Give logic that is not CRUD a package of its own, with no HTTP in it.
- [Background jobs](https://bogie-go.com/docs/jobs.html): Add River with --jobs at new time, or later with g job, and write a worker that runs beside it.
- [Configuration and credentials](https://bogie-go.com/docs/configuration.html): The environment variables, the encrypted settings file, and what staging means here.
- [Your own Postgres](https://bogie-go.com/docs/own-postgres.html): Point the app at a Postgres you already run, without Docker.
- [Testing and CI](https://bogie-go.com/docs/testing.html): Ginkgo and Gomega specs, the test/ folder (testdb, testapp, factories, request specs), what bin/ci runs, and what doctor checks before either does.
- [Deploying](https://bogie-go.com/docs/deploying.html): One Docker image, every role, shipped with Kamal 2 to staging and production.
- [Upgrading an app](https://bogie-go.com/docs/upgrading.html): bogie app:update, a three-way merge to a newer layout that keeps your edits.
- [Conventions and agents](https://bogie-go.com/docs/conventions.html): The six rules every generated app keeps, and why the layout is the way it is.
- [Rails equivalents](https://bogie-go.com/docs/from-rails.html): A lookup table: the Rails names for things, and where each one lives in a generated Bogie app.
- [Command reference](https://bogie-go.com/docs/commands.html): Every Bogie command, every generator and every make target, in one place.
- [Releases](https://bogie-go.com/docs/releases.html): What each Bogie version added or changed, newest first, with breaking changes marked.

## Markdown copies

Every guide as plain Markdown, generated from the same source as the HTML:

<!-- @markdown-copies -->

## Go with AI (free to read online)

Go with AI: Learn Go with Human Mind and Assisted AI, by Roonglit Chareonsupkul. A book, free to read online, that teaches Go to beginners with an AI assistant, using only the standard library and the SURE loop (Specify, Use the AI, Review, Explain). The whole book is free to read online, one page per chapter.

- [Go with AI](https://bogie-go.com/go-with-ai/): the book, its table of contents, editions and prices (free to read online; ebook $0.99 on Kindle and Leanpub and paperback $9.99, coming soon) and a short FAQ.
- [Introduction](https://bogie-go.com/go-with-ai/introduction/): Why learn Go yourself when an AI can write it? The introduction to Go with AI, a book for beginners that's free to read online: who it's for, what you'll build, and the SURE loop for learning Go with AI.
- [Chapter 1: Learning to Code When AI Can Code](https://bogie-go.com/go-with-ai/learn-to-code-with-ai/): How do you start learning Go with an AI assistant? Install Go, set up your project and AI rules file, and write and commit your first Go program, the beginner-friendly way.
- [Chapter 2: Your First Program and Your First Test](https://bogie-go.com/go-with-ai/first-go-program-and-test/): How do you write a test in Go? Turn a plain-English spec into a go test, write your first functions, use a table-driven test, and learn why money is stored in whole cents.
- [Chapter 3: Lists, Lookups and Loops](https://bogie-go.com/go-with-ai/go-slices-maps-loops/): How do slices, maps and loops work in Go? Learn them by building category totals, see why map order is random, and use the AI as a pair programmer that reviews your code.
- [Chapter 4: Modeling Data and Handling Errors](https://bogie-go.com/go-with-ai/go-structs-methods-errors/): How do structs and error handling work in Go? Model data with structs and methods, save and load JSON files, and wrap errors with fmt.Errorf and %w instead of ignoring them.
- [Chapter 5: Organizing Code: Packages and Interfaces](https://bogie-go.com/go-with-ai/go-packages-interfaces/): How do packages and interfaces work in Go? Split a program into packages, define a Storage interface with file and memory versions, and refactor safely with tests while the AI implements.
- [Chapter 6: From Command Line to Web](https://bogie-go.com/go-with-ai/go-web-api-net-http/): How do you build a web API in Go with only the standard library? Write request tests with httptest, let the AI implement a JSON API on net/http, and review its diff line by line.
- [Chapter 7: A Taste of Goroutines](https://bogie-go.com/go-with-ai/go-goroutines-race-detector/): What is a data race in Go, and how do you find one? Send many requests at once, read a race detector report, fix it with a mutex, and build a concurrent import with goroutines.
- [Appendix A: Setting up your AI assistant](https://bogie-go.com/go-with-ai/setup-ai-coding-assistant/): How do you set up Go with an AI coding assistant? Install the Go tools, fix your PATH, pick an editor, install Claude Code, make it read AGENTS.md, and choose safe privacy settings.
- [Appendix B: Just enough Git](https://bogie-go.com/go-with-ai/git-basics/): Which Git commands does a beginner really need? Set up Git, commit each step with a Learned: line, see exactly what the AI changed, and undo changes you don't want.
- [Appendix C: The SURE loop at a glance](https://bogie-go.com/go-with-ai/sure-loop/): What is the SURE loop? A one-page cheat sheet for coding with AI: Specify, Use the AI, Review and Explain, with the check command and how to commit.
- [Appendix D: Review checklists](https://bogie-go.com/go-with-ai/review-checklists/): How do you review code an AI wrote? Every review checklist and 'Where AI gets Go wrong' box from the book in one place, plus how to decide on each AI suggestion.
- [Practice answers](https://bogie-go.com/go-with-ai/answers/): Worked answers to the Go with AI practice exercises: fixing compile errors, slices and maps, error handling, interfaces, a net/http endpoint and a data race, all run on Go 1.27.4.

## Source and design

- [The book](https://bogie-go.com/book.html): Bogie: How to Go from Zero to Production, by Roonglit Chareonsupkul. Kindle and paperback on Amazon.
- [Free chapters](https://bogie-go.com/free-chapters.html): the Introduction and Chapters 1 and 2, the same sample Leanpub offers.
- [Team](https://bogie-go.com/team.html): who builds and maintains Bogie
- [Repository](https://github.com/bogie-go/bogie): the tool, MIT
- [DESIGN.md](https://github.com/bogie-go/bogie/blob/main/docs/DESIGN.md): every decision and its reasoning
- [STATUS.md](https://github.com/bogie-go/bogie/blob/main/docs/STATUS.md): what works today and what is next

## Not

Not a framework, not full-stack (API-only, no views), Postgres only.
